--- title: "Character Personalities" description: "Exploring the GOT" author: - name: Shelby Level url: https://github.com/shelbylevel date: 2-7-2024 categories: [Public Health, SDOH] # self-defined categories #citation: #url: #image: preview-image.png format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 2 toc-location: left self-contained: true #css: css/sl_theme.css draft: true execute: freeze: true --- Evaluation Questions: Do characters of the same GOT houses share similar personality traits? Are there more 'strong' female or male characters in GOT? Do 'strong' characters hold the most power in Westeros? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Read in with tidytuesdayR package # Install from CRAN via: install.packages("tidytuesdayR") # This loads the readme and all the datasets for the week of interest # Either ISO-8601 date or year/week works! library(tidytuesdayR) tuesdata <- tidytuesdayR::tt_load('2022-08-16') #tuesdata <- tidytuesdayR::tt_load(2022, week = 33) characters <- tuesdata$characters myers_briggs <- tuesdata$myers_briggs psych_stats <- tuesdata$psych_stats ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} characters %>% filter( uni_id == 'GOT' ) -> characters_got myers_briggs %>% filter( uni_id == 'GOT' ) -> myers_briggs_got psych_stats %>% filter( uni_id == 'GOT' ) -> psych_stats_got ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} characters <- readr::read_csv( 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2022/2022-08-16/characters.csv' ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Rows: 889 Columns: 7 ── Column specification ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Delimiter: "," chr (6): id, name, uni_id, uni_name, link, image_link dbl (1): notability ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data. ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message. ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} psychometrics <- readr::read_csv( 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2022/2022-08-16/psych_stats.csv' ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Rows: 356489 Columns: 10 ── Column specification ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Delimiter: "," chr (6): char_id, char_name, uni_id, uni_name, question, personality dbl (4): avg_rating, rank, rating_sd, number_ratings ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data. ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message. ``` ::: ::: # Data wrangling ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Network to see similarities between GOT characters? # set seed set.seed(4321) ``` ::: # Intersection ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} psycho_df <- psychometrics %>% dplyr::filter(uni_name == "Game of Thrones" & avg_rating >= 80) %>% dplyr::group_by(char_name, question) %>% dplyr::slice_max(order_by = avg_rating, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% dplyr::ungroup() %>% dplyr::group_by(question) %>% dplyr::mutate( question_id = dplyr::cur_group_id(), personality = stringr::str_c(question_id, personality, sep = "_") ) %>% dplyr::ungroup() %>% dplyr::select(char_name, question, personality) %>% dplyr::group_by(char_name) %>% dplyr::summarise(personality = list(as.character(personality))) %>% dplyr::rename("from" = "char_name") %>% tidyr::crossing(dplyr::rename( ., "to" = "from", "personality_to" = "personality" )) %>% dplyr::mutate( frequency = purrr::map2_dbl( personality, personality_to, ~ length(base::intersect(.x, .y)) ) ) %>% dplyr::select(from, to, frequency) %>% dplyr::filter(from != to) %>% dplyr::mutate( similarity = case_when( frequency <= quantile(frequency, probs = 0.80) ~ "q80", frequency <= quantile(frequency, probs = 0.90) ~ "q90", frequency <= quantile(frequency, probs = 0.95) ~ "q95", frequency <= quantile(frequency, probs = 0.99) ~ "q99", TRUE ~ "Top1" ) ) %>% dplyr::arrange(frequency) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dplyr::mutate(house = case_when( str_detect(char_name, 'Stark') ~ 'Stark', str_detect(char_name, 'Snow') ~ 'Stark', str_detect(char_name, 'Greyjoy') ~ 'Greyjoy', str_detect(char_name, 'Tarth') ~ 'Tarth', str_detect(char_name, 'Bronn') ~ 'Blackwater', str_detect(char_name, 'Lannister') ~ 'Lannister', str_detect(char_name, 'Targaryen') ~ 'Targaryen', str_detect(char_name, 'Seaworth') ~ 'Seaworth', str_detect(char_name, 'Baratheon') ~ 'Baratheon', str_detect(char_name, 'Mormont') ~ 'Mormont', str_detect(char_name, 'Tyrell') ~ 'Tyrell', str_detect(char_name, 'Martell') ~ 'Martell', str_detect(char_name, 'Baelish') ~ 'Baelish', str_detect(char_name, 'Tarly') ~ 'Tarly', str_detect(char_name, 'Clegane') ~ 'Clegane' )) %>% ``` ::: # Network ## Network vertices ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} psycho_ve <- psycho_df %>% dplyr::group_by(to) %>% dplyr::summarise(links = sum(frequency)) %>% dplyr::select(to, links) %>% dplyr::mutate( house = case_when( str_detect(to, 'Stark') ~ 'Stark', str_detect(to, 'Snow') ~ 'Stark', str_detect(to, 'Greyjoy') ~ 'Greyjoy', str_detect(to, 'Tarth') ~ 'Tarth', str_detect(to, 'Bronn') ~ 'Blackwater', str_detect(to, 'Lannister') ~ 'Lannister', str_detect(to, 'Targaryen') ~ 'Targaryen', str_detect(to, 'Seaworth') ~ 'Seaworth', str_detect(to, 'Baratheon') ~ 'Baratheon', str_detect(to, 'Mormont') ~ 'Mormont', str_detect(to, 'Tyrell') ~ 'Tyrell', str_detect(to, 'Martell') ~ 'Martell', str_detect(to, 'Baelish') ~ 'Baelish', str_detect(to, 'Tarly') ~ 'Tarly', str_detect(to, 'Clegane') ~ 'Clegane' ) ) ``` ::: ## Network object ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} psycho_ig <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame( d = psycho_df, vertices = psycho_ve, directed = FALSE ) ``` ::: ## Network tidy ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} psycho_tg <- tidygraph::as_tbl_graph(psycho_ig) %>% tidygraph::activate(nodes) %>% dplyr::mutate(label = name) size <- igraph::V(psycho_tg)$links ``` ::: # Legend Annotation ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} data_label <- tibble( x = seq(1.75, 2.25, length.out = 30), y = seq(-1.35, -1.35, length.out = 30), color = psycho_ve %>% pull(links) %>% sort(), alpha = psycho_ve %>% pull(links) %>% sort(), size = psycho_ve %>% pull(links) %>% sort() ) ``` ::: # Plot aesthetics ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} background <- "#141C26" lines_color <- "#A6444C" title_color <- "#F2C230" In total, the project collects information on more than 2,000 characters, with 400 descriptive adjectives rated on a scale of 1 to 100, depending on how strongly one would identify the character's particular characteristic. characters? # set seed set.seed(4321) ``` ::: ## Intersection ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} psycho_stark <- psychometrics %>% dplyr::filter( uni_name == "Game of Thrones" & grepl('Stark|Snow', char_name) & avg_rating >= 80 ) %>% dplyr::group_by(char_name, question) %>% dplyr::slice_max(order_by = avg_rating, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% dplyr::ungroup() %>% dplyr::group_by(question) %>% dplyr::mutate( question_id = dplyr::cur_group_id(), personality = stringr::str_c(question_id, personality, sep = "_") ) %>% dplyr::ungroup() %>% dplyr::select(char_name, question, personality) %>% dplyr::group_by(char_name) %>% dplyr::summarise(personality = list(as.character(personality))) %>% dplyr::rename("from" = "char_name") %>% tidyr::crossing(dplyr::rename( ., "to" = "from", "personality_to" = "personality" )) %>% dplyr::mutate( frequency = purrr::map2_dbl( personality, personality_to, ~ length(base::intersect(.x, .y)) ) ) %>% dplyr::select(from, to, frequency) %>% dplyr::filter(from != to) %>% dplyr::mutate( similarity = case_when( frequency <= quantile(frequency, probs = 0.80) ~ "q80", frequency <= quantile(frequency, probs = 0.90) ~ "q90", frequency <= quantile(frequency, probs = 0.95) ~ "q95", frequency <= quantile(frequency, probs = 0.99) ~ "q99", TRUE ~ "Top1" ) ) %>% dplyr::arrange(frequency) ``` ::: ## Network ### Network vertices ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} psycho_stark_ve <- psycho_stark %>% dplyr::group_by(to) %>% dplyr::summarise(links = sum(frequency)) %>% dplyr::select(to, links) ``` ::: ### Network object ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} psycho_stark_ig <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame( d = psycho_stark, vertices = psycho_stark_ve, directed = FALSE ) ``` ::: ### Network tidy ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} psycho_stark_tg <- tidygraph::as_tbl_graph(psycho_stark_ig) %>% tidygraph::activate(nodes) %>% dplyr::mutate(label = name) size <- igraph::V(psycho_stark_tg)$links ``` ::: ## Legend Annotation ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} data_label <- tibble( x = seq(1.75, 2.25, length.out = 7), y = seq(-1.35, -1.35, length.out = 7), color = psycho_stark_ve %>% pull(links) %>% sort(), alpha = psycho_stark_ve %>% pull(links) %>% sort(), size = psycho_stark_ve %>% pull(links) %>% sort() ) ``` ::: ## Plot aesthetics ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} background <- "#141C26" lines_color <- "#A6444C" title_color <- "#F2C230" subtitle_color <- "#FFAB16" text_color <- "#F2F2F2" caption_color <- "#6C7D8C" ``` ::: ## Annotation ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} annotation_title_text <- c("House Stark") annotation_text <- c( "The Open-Source Psychometrics Project, it has recruited more than 3 million volunteers to rate characters from different series, according to 400 descriptive adjectives and other properties. The responses can be aggregated to create profiles that users can match as part of a personality test. In total, the project collects information on more than 2,000 characters, with 400 descriptive adjectives rated on a scale of 1 to 100, depending on how strongly one would identify the character's particular characteristic. From the data set, GOT characters have been selected, to investigate which characters share the greatest number of the strongest characteristics (rating >80%) in common or similarity." ) annotation_text <- stringr::str_wrap(annotation_text, 70) %>% stringr::str_replace_all("\n", "
